Article Title: 'Disappointed with PM Modi': Shehzad Poonawalla’s sarcastic 'dictator' jibe at oppn after quitting BJP
Article Text:
Shehzad Poonawalla; PM Narendra Modi

NEW DELHI: A day after resigning from the party, former BJP national spokesperson Shehzad Poonawalla on Saturday released an Instagram video saying he was “disappointed” with Prime Minister Narendra Modi In a sarcastic jibe at the Congress and its most prominent face, leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi , Poonawalla said that unlike Congress prime ministers, PM Modi, despite being in office for 12 years, was still to become a “dictator."Poonawalla’s remarks came after PM Modi, in his fifth Instagram video since the recent student protests in Delhi, said he had “forgiven” protesters who allegedly abused him and his late mother during the agitation. Several people, mostly youngsters, were booked for allegedly abusing the PM and his mother, after the protests ended with the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan as Union education minister on July 25.“I am completely disappointed with Prime Minister Narendra Modi. It has been 12 years and he has still not learnt how to be a dictator,” Poonawalla said in his Hindi video, adding that instead of becoming a dictator, the prime minister appealed for those who abused him to be forgiven.He urged the prime minister to learn “real dictatorship” from former prime ministers Indira Gandhi and Jawaharlal Nehru, Rahul Gandhi’s grandmother and great-grandfather, respectively. Poonawalla, a former Congress member, also referred to cases filed against students in Congress-ruled Karnataka and Kerala.He further referred to the alleged curbing of free speech during Nehru’s tenure and invoked the Emergency imposed by Indira Gandhi in 1975.“Who got all parliamentarians put in jail? Indira Gandhi. Who ordered police to fire at seers? Indira Gandhi,” Poonawalla remarked.The second incident he referred to appeared to be a reference to the 1966 police firing on protesters outside Parliament during a demonstration demanding a nationwide ban on cow slaughter.The former BJP spokesperson also referred to several protest movements that he alleged were “crushed” by Congress governments at the Centre and in various states.“We saw during the 2011 Anna Hazare agitation that 1,200-1,300 people were arrested. Anna Hazare himself was arrested. Rajbala lost her life,” he remarked, referring to the anti-corruption movement led by activist Anna Hazare that had put the then Congress-led UPA government under pressure.Rajbala was a woman protester who died following a Delhi Police crackdown at Ramlila Ground during the agitation.“Come on, Modi ji. It has been 12 years and you have still not become a dictator. You have poured water on the hopes of the Left-liberals,” Poonawalla concluded.PM Modi’s Instagram videos have been described as an attempt by the prime minister to reach out to “Gen Z” — the demographic with the largest participation in the recent student protests.
Article Summary: Former BJP national spokesperson Shehzad Poonawalla released an Instagram video saying he was “disappointed” with Prime Minister Narendra Modi. He said that unlike Congress prime ministers, PM Modi was still to become a “dictator"

Legendary Nepal-born mountaineer Nirmal “Nims Dai” Purja has died after an avalanche struck his expedition on Broad Peak in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir, ending a two-day search operation. Article Title: 'First you broke their bones, now filing FIRs': Rahul Gandhi warns PM Modi, Amit Shah to not 'threaten Gen Z into silence'
Article Text:
Rahul Gandhi took a jab at PM Modi and Amit Shah, calling them 'India's past'

NEW DELHI: Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Friday targeted Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah over the action against student protesters, alleging that the government was trying to "silence Gen Z" through FIRs and social media takedowns after directly attacking them during protests.Making a statement on X, the Congress leader said, "PM Modi and Amit Shah - you cannot threaten Gen Z into silence. First you broke their bones. Now you are filing FIRs and taking down their accounts."Further taking a jab at PM Modi and Shah, he added, "You are India’s past. Be careful about how you treat India’s future."This comes a day after Rahul demanded a Supreme Court-monitored, high-powered committee to investigate the alleged police action against student protesters during the July 20 demonstration at Delhi's Jantar Mantar.In a post on X, the Congress MP had called for an impartial probe into the alleged use of force, saying, "Students deserve justice. An independent SC-monitored high-powered committee must be constituted to probe brutalities against our students."Gandhi also shared a video purportedly showing police action against the protesters. The footage appeared to show police personnel lathi-charging demonstrators, while another clip showed a man in civilian clothes forcefully pushing a student carrying the Indian flag onto the road.His demand came as Opposition MPs from several INDIA bloc parties staged a protest at Makar Dwar in the Parliament complex over the alleged police action against students and the alleged embezzlement of donations meant for the Ram Temple in Ayodhya.The MPs gathered around 10.30 am, carrying placards questioning who ordered the police action at Jantar Mantar and raising slogans demanding accountability from the Centre over the alleged use of force and the alleged financial irregularities in donations to the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Temple.The protest took place hours before the Rajya Sabha was scheduled to consider and pass the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026.
Article Summary: Rahul Gandhi accuses PM Modi and Amit Shah of trying to "silence Gen Z" through FIRs and social media takedowns after directly attacking them during protests. This comes a day after Rahul demanded a Supreme Court-monitored, high-powered committee to investigate the alleged police action.

Article Title: Parts of Manusmriti now part of 'curriculum', says Mallikarjun Kharge
Article Text:
Rajya Sabha LoP Mallikarjun Kharge speaks in Rajya Sabha during the Monsoon Session of Parliament, in New Delhi

NEW DELHI: The debate on Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill in RS Thursday turned into a heated argument between treasury benches and opposition when leader of the opposition Mallikarjun Kharge read out what he claimed Hindi translation of a portion from Manusmriti.Kharge alleged portions of Manusmriti have become part of the "curriculum" under BJP govt. He was challenged by leader of the House J P Nadda, who asked the LoP to produce the "original manuscript" for authentication.RS chairperson CP Radhakrishnan asked Kharge what Manusmriti had to do with the bill. Kharge claimed, "Manusmriti teaches that if a 'Shudra' listens to Veda, his ears should be filled with shards; if he reads Ved aloud, his tongue should be cut off; and if he retains its words, his body should be dismembered."BJP MP Sudhanshu Trivedi slammed Kharge citing B R Ambedkar's writings to argue there was no untouchability in the era of Manu.
Article Summary: Opposition leader of the opposition Mallikarjun Kharge read out what he claimed Hindi translation of a portion from Manusmriti. He was challenged by leader of House J P Nadda, who asked the LoP to produce the "original manuscript" for authentication.

Article Title: BJP trying to force Muslims, minorities to worship Hindu deities, says Owaisi; DMK slams Vande Mataram bill as 'fraud'
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: AIMIM leader Asaduddin Owaisi Thursday slammed the bill making “insult” to Vande Mataram a crime, saying BJP is trying to force Muslims and minorities to worship Hindu deities, while DMK claimed it was hurting the secular fabric of the country.DMK MP A Raja, who moved an amendment to the bill in Lok Sabha, called the legislation a “fraud” perpetrated by Modi govt on people. He said Constituent Assembly approved only two paragraphs of the song. “The Constitution came from Constituent Assembly, and it is unconstitutional to exceed Constituent Assembly. This bill will not stand judicial scrutiny. This is against the secular fabric of India and we will not accept it,” he said.Meanwhile, as Congress attacked govt for passing the bill amid din, MP KC Venugopal questioned the absence of home minister Amit Shah from LS when his ministry’s legislation to “prevent the insult to national symbols” was taken up. Manickam Tagore too criticised Shah’s absence from the House. Some members of Congress — which has been asking Shah questions about the police crackdown on student protesters — termed the bill as “divisive” and against secularism.Owaisi argued “national anthem — Jana Gana Mana” is a reflection of the country and its people, but Vande Mataram is about prayers to “devi-devta”. “This bill is a grave violation of Article 25 that gives freedom of religion. This is intended to convert India into a Hindu theocratic state.”Congress MP Tariq Anwar said govt should have taken opposition parties into confidence for this bill but “this govt tries to impose its views on people”.He said Vande Mataram was a principal song of the freedom struggle, and all Congress functions start with the national song. “But controversy is about govt interfering with the decision of Constituent Assembly...objectionable words were removed because India is secular.” Party MP Ujjwal Raman Singh called the bill’s passage without discussion a “black day” in India’s history.
Article Summary: AIMIM leader Asaduddin Owaisi slammed the bill making “insult’ to Vande Mataram a crime. DMK MP A Raja called the legislation a “fraud” perpetrated by Modi govt on people.

Article Title: NEET leak row: Opposition politicising issue, government has brought in strict law, says BJP
Article Text:
BJP MP Sudhanshu Trivedi speaks in the Rajya Sabha during the Monsoon session of Parliament, in New Delhi

NEW DELHI: Treasury bench MPs condemned opposition for politicising the NEET-UG paper leak issue and recent protests, as they highlighted how govt has taken steps in the right direction to address concerns by holding dialogue with students to end their agitation and proposing a stronger law against exam paper leaks.Participating in the discussion, BJP MP Sudhanshu Trivedi listed government's efforts to resolve student protest and also highlighted how senior ministers J P Nadda and Jitendra Singh held talks with them and activist Sonam Wangchuk, who was fasting for 26 days.Government agreed to the demands of students, he said, adding Dharmendra Pradhan resigned as education minister, a fast-track court was set up and a task force was set up by PM Narendra Modi under Aadhaar architect Nandan Nilekani.On Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, Trivedi said there are three basic principles - a sensitive approach towards students, a secured process and a stringent law against paper leaks. Trivedi said the bill provides for stringent punishment, time-bound investigation and speedier justice. These will prove key in preventing paper leaks, he said.Targeting opposition MPs, who raised questions on PM Modi's educational qualifications, he said those who have never themselves faced competition in exams, in education, or in their own political parties are now teaching the govt. "In contrast, our politicians and our PM have faced competition and exams and have risen from the ground," Trivedi said.JDU's Sanjay Jha supported the bill, saying this should not be looked at from political prospects.Shiv Sena's Milind Deora suggested students should be involved in the reform process by giving them a formal role in the consultations.
Article Summary: Treasury bench MPs condemned opposition for politicising the NEET-UG paper leak issue and recent protests. They highlighted how govt has taken steps in the right direction to address concerns. BJP MP Sudhanshu Trivedi listed government's efforts to resolve student protest.

Article Title: Complaint filed against MP Pappu Yadav over Parliament protest on Ram Mandir donation 'theft' row
Article Text:
Complaint filed against Purnia MP Pappu Yadav in Delhi over Parliament protest





NEW DELHI: A complaint has been filed against Independent Purnia MP Rajesh Ranjan alias Pappu Yadav at Delhi's Jehangirpuri Police Station over his protest inside the Parliament complex on the alleged Ram Mandir donation embezzlement issue, as reported by news agency ANI.The complaint, lodged by Surya Maithil, accuses Yadav of hurting religious sentiments during the demonstration. Maithil also alleged that several INDIA bloc MPs backed the protest.Claiming that Yadav insulted religious symbols, Maithil said, "The way Pappu Yadav insulted the saffron today and staged the drama outside Parliament, supported by Rahul Gandhi, Dimple Yadav, Awadhesh Kumar and other INDIA alliance MPs, has hurt the sentiments of Sanatanis. During the protest, he even placed a picture of Lord Ram Lalla Virajman under his feet."He said he had sought immediate legal action against Yadav and others, urging Union home minister Amit Shah , the Delhi Police commissioner and other senior police officials to act on the complaint.On Thursday, the Parliament complex witnessed an unusual opposition protest in the form of a street play over the alleged Ram Mandir donation "theft" row.Opposition MPs also demanded that Amit Shah address Parliament over the recent police action against protesting students.Amid slogans of "Chanda chor, gaddi chhod", "Jawab tumko dena hoga" and "Amit Shah, sadan mein aao", Pappu Yadav, dressed as a temple priest in saffron robes, carried a photograph of Lord Ram and enacted a symbolic performance. As fellow opposition MPs, playing devotees, dropped donations into a collection box, Yadav was shown pocketing the money instead, before another MP confronted him in the staged act.(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: Complaint filed against Purnia MP Pappu Yadav in Delhi over Parliament protest. Yadav dressed as a temple priest in saffron robes and enacted a symbolic performance. As fellow opposition MPs dropped donations into a collection box, Yadav was shown pocketing the money.

Article Title: 'Wrong name, age in FIR': Advocate for Noida girl booked over 'abusive' video on PM Modi
Article Text:
Advocate Anil Singh, representing the Noida resident booked over allegedly objectionable remarks against Prime Minister Narendra Modi, claimed that the FIR was registered under the wrong name and age.





NEW DELHI: Advocate Anil Singh, representing the Noida resident booked over allegedly objectionable remarks against Prime Minister Narendra Modi, claimed that the FIR was registered under the wrong name and incorrectly states that she works at a salon.Ruchika Singh allegedly made defamatory remarks against Prime Minister Narendra Modi during the CJP protest at Jantar Mantar in Delhi.Speaking to IANS, Anil said she is actually 15 years old and is pursuing Class 10 through open schooling."The FIR has been registered under the wrong name. Her actual age is 15 years. I have read the FIR, which states that she works at a salon. However, she is currently 15 years old and is pursuing Class 10 through open schooling," Singh said.He alleged that the FIR was registered without any investigation and that the police acted in haste."The FIR was registered without any investigation. The police have also acted in great haste. We have not received any notice from the police yet. So far, no police personnel have contacted us, nor has any pressure been put on us," Anil said.Noida Police had earlier registered a Zero FIR against Ruchika following a complaint by Supreme Court advocate Smriti Singh.The case was registered under Sections 352, 353(1), and 356(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) over allegedly objectionable remarks against the prime minister during the CJP protest at Jantar Mantar.The matter was later transferred to Delhi Police as the alleged incident took place during the protest in the national capital.The girl later posted a video apologising for the remarks and claimed that she was 15 years old. She said she had been influenced by other protesters and apologised for what she had said.Prime Minister Narendra Modi also spoke about the incident in an Instagram video, calling the remarks directed at him and his late mother a "cultural shock". He appealed against punitive action and said young people should be embraced rather than punished.
Article Summary: Ruchika Singh allegedly made defamatory remarks against Prime Minister Narendra Modi during the CJP protest at Jantar Mantar in Delhi. Advocate Anil Singh, representing the Noida resident, claimed that the FIR was registered under the wrong name and age. He said she is actually 15 years old and is pursuing Class 10 through open schooling.

Article Title: 'Abusing not a crime': CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke slams FIR against Noida woman, recalls UP CM video
Article Text:
CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke (Image Credit: X)





NEW DELHI: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke has questioned the registration of an FIR against a woman accused of using abusive language against Prime Minister Narendra Modi He asked whether there were "two laws" in the country and why similar action was not taken against BJP leaders and IT cell members accused of using objectionable language.In a video shared on 'X', Dipke said he had learnt that a case had been registered against a woman for using abusive language and questioned why similar action had not been taken in other cases.Also read: Noida woman apologises over PM Modi 'abuse' video, claims she was 'influenced' “If you are registering cases for abusing, when will cases be registered against those BJP IT cell people who have been using abusive language for women online for years?” Dipke asked.He alleged that several such social media users had repeatedly used objectionable language against women while openly identifying themselves with the BJP.“They have been using all kinds of words, not respecting women from any angle. And they proudly wrote in their bio, ‘Followed by PM Modi’. Such people have abused girls. When will the case be filed on them?” he added.Dipke also referred to remarks made by BJP leaders in the past, questioning why similar action had not been taken against them.“It is not just the BJP's IT cell. Their Member of Parliament, Ramesh Bidhuri ji, what words did he use for a fellow Member of Parliament, everyone remembers that,” he said.He also cited Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath, alleging that a video had surfaced in which he used abusive language against a camera person.“The CM of UP even had a video, where he had abused a camera person. So, what is going on? Are there two laws in this country? There is a separate law for youth and a separate law for BJP and their leaders,” he said.Claiming that abusive language was not a criminal offence, Dipke said cases should not be filed merely over such remarks.“Abusing is not a crime. It is a bad thing, explain it to the person that they should not use such language, but why is a case being filed? If cases are to be filed for abusing, highest number of cases will be filed against the BJP's IT cell, because they are the ones who have abused women the most. And it will be against BJP's leaders, who have used bad language for years, even inside the Parliament,” he said.In a post accompanying the video, CJP said: “Will an FIR be filed against all those IT Cell members who have been abusing women for the last several years?”The remarks came a day after a Zero FIR was registered at the Expressway police station in Noida against Ruchika Singh for allegedly using abusive and objectionable language against Prime Minister Narendra Modi during a protest at Jantar Mantar on July 23.The FIR was lodged on the complaint of Ghaziabad resident Smriti Singh under Sections 352 (intentional insult to provoke breach of peace), 353(1) (statements conducing to public mischief) and 356(1) (defamation) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.Police said the Zero FIR would be transferred to New Delhi for further investigation.
Article Summary: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke questioned the registration of an FIR against a woman accused of using abusive language against Prime Minister Narendra Modi. He asked whether there were "two laws" in the country and why similar action was not taken against BJP leaders and IT cell members.

Article Title: Forest officer held for accepting Rs 5 lakh in bribe
Article Text: Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar: The anti-corruption bureau (ACB) on Friday arrested a divisional forest officer from Beed for allegedly accepting Rs 5 lakh as part of a Rs 45 lakh bribe demand in exchange for releasing plantation funds and extending official favours to a subordinate officer.Police identified the accused as Srinivas Linganna Lakhmawad (40), divisional forest officer, social forestry division, Beed. The complaint was lodged on Thursday by a forest range officer.Superintendent of police Madhuri Kedar Kangane said, “The accused demanded Rs 45 lakh from a forest range officer for facilitating the release of plantation funds, refraining from pursuing a suspension proposal against him, securing two pending annual salary increments and halting an inquiry into nursery-related works. After verification of the complaint, a trap was laid and he was caught while accepting Rs 5 lakh in cash. ”Additional SP Shashikant Shingare said the trap was executed on Friday by a team led by inspector Bhaskar Navale of the Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar ACB unit at Lakhmawad’s residence in Urja Heights on Canal Road near Nagar Naka in Beed.The police said the accused attended the DPDC meeting during the day and reached home after the meeting for receiving the bribe amount from his subordinate. A case has been registered against the accused under Section 7 of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988.
Article Summary: Police identified the accused as Srinivas Linganna Lakhmawad (40), divisional forest officer, social forestry division, Beed. The complaint was lodged on Thursday by a forest range officer. A trap was laid and he was caught while accepting Rs 5 lakh in cash.

Article Title: Man’s body found floating in river
Article Text:
The body of a Athul, a functionary of Shiv Sena party was recovered from the Thamirabarani river near Kuzhithurai in Kanyakumari district on Friday





Madurai: The body of a 30-year-old history-sheeter from Kerala was recovered from Thamirabarani river near Kannankodu in Kuzhithurai on Friday, prompting police to investigate whether he was murdered and his body later dumped in the water.Police said local residents alerted them after spotting a decomposed body floating in the river. It was retrieved and identified as that of Athul, 30, a native of Thiruvananthapuram . Preliminary inquiries revealed that he had died nearly three days ago. Investigators noticed tattoos related to Shiva Sena on his body, and also injuries, raising suspicions of foul play.The body was sent to Kanyakumari Govt Medical College Hospital for postmortem. Meanwhile, Athul's car was traced to Chitharal in Kanyakumari district. His driving licence, Aadhaar card, and other personal documents were inside. Kaliakkavilai police have registered a case and are investigating. Police said he was a history sheeter and had various cases pending with Kerala police.
Article Summary: The body of a 30-year-old history-sheeter from Kerala was recovered from Thamirabarani river near Kannankodu in Kuzhithurai on Friday. Preliminary inquiries revealed that he had died nearly three days ago. Police said he was a history sheeter and had various cases pending with Kerala police.

Article Title: Truck driver dies in road accident near Salem
Article Text: SALEM: A driver died in an accident involving a truck, a pickup van and a bus near Mecheri in Salem district on Wednesday. More than 10 bus passengers suffered injuries in the accident.According to the Mecheri police, a TNSTC bus carrying 51 passengers was heading to Karur from Mettur when a speeding pickup van attempted to overtake it. “The pickup van collided head-on with a truck coming from the opposite direction,” said an officer at the Mecheri police station. The truck grazed the bus, shattering its windows and injuring more than 10 passengers seated near the windows.Truck driver C Penumoola Revanthra, 53 of Guntur in Andhra Pradesh died on the spot. The injured were rushed to govt hospitals in Mettur and Omalur.Fire service personnel, assisted by Mecheri police and residents, worked to move the damaged truck and pickup van to the roadside. Traffic on the Mettur–Salem highway was disrupted for an hour.The Mecheri police registered a case.
Article Summary: More than 10 bus passengers suffered injuries in the accident. Truck driver C Penumoola Revanthra, 53 of Guntur in Andhra Pradesh died on the spot. Traffic on the Mettur–Salem highway was disrupted for an hour.
